A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SILO-BENCH and contain the corresponding main sections, seven figures, 18 tables, and Appendices A–H. Text and rendered pages support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 54 configurations across 30 tasks, totaling 1,620 experiments, plus single-agent comparisons, failure analyses, and prompt-scaffold ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the measured performance in Tables 1–4 and the detailed results and analyses in Appendices F–H.

M1.justification: The task-generation procedure, data partitioning, agent initialization, round-based execution, and three communication protocols are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same prompts.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 30 algorithmic tasks across aggregation, mesh-network, and global-shuffle levels. Table 9 retains all task specifications; the new image-generation mention concerns related work only.

E2.justification: The evaluated models remain DeepSeek-V3.1, GPT-OSS-120B, and Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B under BP, P2P, and SFS. Single-agent controls and scaffold comparators are retained; the newly cited works are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Agent scales, 128K context windows, the 100-round limit, metrics, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Appendix C.3 changes reported compute accounting without establishing a changed experimental budget or rerun.

E4.justification: The communication heatmaps, token-feasibility analysis, failure cases, leader-emergence analysis, successful coordination examples, and three prompt-scaffold ablations are retained without substantive revisions.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2 still specifies one execution per configuration with fixed data-generation seeds. The annotation agreement, standard-deviation summaries, and percentile reporting are unchanged; no repeated-run or uncertainty analysis is added.

E6.justification: Benchmark scores, rankings, plots, and ablation entries are unchanged. However, Appendix C.3 changes 500+ GPU-hours equivalent from total compute to compute for each experiment, revising the scope of a quantitative resource-cost estimate.

T1.justification: The task and metric definitions in Equations 1–5, communication-complexity characterizations, Relative Coordination Cost formula, and formal protocol specifications are unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a role-agnostic benchmark, a 54-configuration empirical study, and a Communication-Reasoning Gap that worsens with scale and task complexity. Abstract and conclusion edits do not change these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning information integration, coordination overhead, protocol suitability, and emergent-leader bottlenecks are retained. The limitations concerning protocol coverage, homogeneous teams, and model selection are unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code repository link in the abstract. Appendix C.3 changes the compute estimate from 500+ GPU-hours overall to that amount per experiment; other implementation and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Ma et al. (2025), Talk2image, as an interactive image-generation example and Su et al. (2026), Difficulty-aware agentic orchestration, alongside Mixture-of-Agents. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Limited wording and punctuation edits replace several em dashes, refine terminology, and enumerate the three experimental axes. A corresponding-author email is added; section order and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: All figures and tables are retained without redesign. Tables 6–8 are rearranged within the appendix, and text and references reflow, shifting the subsequent appendix pagination.

improvement.justification: The new code-access pointer provides a concrete aid to locating the implementation, modestly improving reproducibility information. Scientific evidence is unchanged. This limited benefit is tempered by the unexplained switch from total to per-experiment compute in Appendix C.3.
